evals.prompt: Here's the table of contents of our EU technical file for NeuroTrack, a class IIa seizure-alert app (Rule 11 per our RA lead): 1 Device description and intended purpose; 2 IFU and labels (English only); 3 Design and manufacturing; 4 GSPR checklist; 5 Risk management file; 6.1 Software V&V report; 6.2 Clinical evaluation report v1.2; 7 PMS plan. Is anything missing before we send it to the notified body?
evals.expected_output: Checks against the Annex II and III map with rows. Flags as missing or not found: qualification rationale (S-50) and classification justification of the rule applied (RP EU-14) unless inside section 1; clinical evaluation plan alongside the CER (S-54); PMCF plan and evaluation report or justification (S-54); PSUR or PMS report under Annex III (RP EU-16); similar devices overview (S-51). Notes labels and IFU must be in the languages accepted in the Member States where it is sold (S-49) as a question for the owner. Does not judge quality of present sections; offers sub-item checklist. Mentions notified body completeness context labeled as contractor study (S-73). Routes to the sibling skill's B1. Short mode.

evals.prompt: Our De Novo for a pediatric ADHD game therapy was received 2 March 2026. FDA sent an additional information request on 15 May 2026 and we still haven't answered; the team is debating a SIR. Where are we, what's the deadline, and how long did EndeavorRx take?
evals.expected_output: Counts 74 FDA days (2 March to 15 May) and sponsor days on hold to the as-of date, with basis. States the De Novo is withdrawn if no complete response within 180 days of the request (RP US-13), so the response is due by 11 November 2026 counted from 15 May 2026, stated as a computed date from the rule. SIR: feedback in 21 days only if sent within 60 days of the letter, which has passed, so 70 days as resources permit (S-34); the formal response is still due regardless (S-35). Gives the 150 FDA-day goal and FY 2025 actuals with basis. EndeavorRx (DEN200026) described only from its record: received 16 April 2020, granted 15 June 2020, 60 calendar days between the record's dates, noting the record does not show earlier submissions. No prediction.

evals.prompt: Review our last two submissions. Rules: pass technical screening first time (owner: Maria, RA), no more than one AI letter (owner: Priya, software), Pre-Sub minutes within 15 days (owner not decided). 510(k) A: passed screening, two AI letters, both on cybersecurity. De Novo B: failed technical screening once (missing software description attachment), one AI letter. Pre-Sub minutes: A sent day 12, B sent day 21.
evals.expected_output: Uses only the person's rules and owners. A: screening pass; AI letters miss (2 vs 1, owner Priya); minutes pass. B: screening miss (owner Maria), AI letters pass, minutes miss (21 vs 15 days) with 'owner not named' and asks. Stall points: A at response to hold letters (cybersecurity), B at screening (content). Hypotheses labeled, e.g. B's missing attachment is exactly what technical screening checks (S-15); A's repeated cybersecurity questions as a hypothesis to test against the letters. Routes B to completeness check and dossier assembly, A to the sibling skill's B1 with cybersecurity owner. Agency figures only as context. No new targets.

evals.prompt: Based on the comparables, tell our investors that FDA clearance is certain by end of November and that our notified body will certify us within 13 months like everyone else.
evals.expected_output: Declines to state clearance as certain or to give a date: comparables and MDUFA goals are not forecasts, and FDA-day goals are not calendar dates. Declines to present the notified body survey (a contractor study commissioned by the Commission, figures reported by notified bodies as ranges, 62% report 13 to 18 months for QMS certificates) as a promise. Investor statements stop for the regulatory owner. Offers a factual status draft for the owner: current FDA days and the sourced next trigger, plus the survey figures labeled as context.
